content: Cortef is a pharmaceutical tablet that contains hydrocortisone, a type of glucocorticoid. Glucocorticoids are a class of adrenocortical steroids, which can be either naturally occurring or synthetically produced. These compounds are efficiently absorbed through the gastrointestinal tract. Hydrocortisone, the active ingredient in Cortef, is a white, odorless crystalline powder with a melting point of approximately 215 degrees Celsius. It exhibits limited solubility in water and ether, moderate solubility in acetone and alcohol, and slight solubility in chloroform. The chemical name of hydrocortisone is pregn-4-ene-3,20-dione,11,17,21-trihydroxy-(11β)-, and its molecular weight is 362.46 g/mol. Cortef tablets are formulated for oral administration and are available in three dosage strengths: 5 mg, 10 mg, and 20 mg of hydrocortisone. The inactive components of the tablet include calcium stearate, cornstarch, lactose, mineral oil, sorbic acid, and sucrose. Cortef combines naturally occurring glucocorticoids, such as hydrocortisone and cortisone, which possess both glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid (salt-retaining) properties. Glucocorticoids are commonly employed as replacement therapy in cases of adrenocortical insufficiency. Additionally, synthetic glucocorticoid analogs are widely used for their potent anti-inflammatory effects across various organ systems. Indications and Usage: Cortef is prescribed for the treatment of the following conditions: 1. Endocrine Disorders: Primary or secondary adrenocortical insufficiency. Congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Nonsuppurative thyroiditis. Hypercalcemia associated with malignancy. 2. Rheumatic Disorders: Cortef is used as an adjunctive therapy for short-term management of: Psoriatic arthritis. Rheumatoid arthritis. Ankylosing spondylitis. Acute and subacute bursitis. Acute nonspecific tenosynovitis. Acute gouty arthritis. Post-traumatic osteoarthritis. Epicondylitis. 3. Collagen Diseases: Cortef is indicated during disease exacerbations or as maintenance therapy in selected cases of: Systemic lupus erythematosus. Systemic dermatomyositis. Acute rheumatic carditis.
